assumptions: PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, S3, and reset are modeled as parent-scoped events rather than persistent input variables because the NL describes them as triggers/signals.
hbrg is encoded as int values: 1 for upward drive, -1 for downward drive, and 0 for stop. The NL requires distinction but does not specify numeric encoding.

The phrase 'immediately checks the next destination' is represented by entering floor states with outgoing request-triggered transitions; no additional decision pseudostate was added because the NL did not list one.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init verifies initial dispatch to floor 1 with stop hbrg, then an arrival sensor alone does not move the controller from F1.
scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_stop_and_sensor_no_fire

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes F1 request to floor 2, MU2 arrival at F2, then immediate next request from F2 upward to MU3.
scenario_results.name: f1_ps2_mu2_arrive_f2_continue_mu3

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes direct travel from F1 to F3, arrival stop at F3, then request for floor 2 drives downward through MD2 to F2.
scenario_results.name: f1_ps3_mu3_arrive_f3_then_md2_to_f2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes the F2 request for floor 1 downward branch and S1 arrival back to F1 stop.
scenario_results.name: f2_ps1_md1_arrive_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes the distinct F3 request for floor 1 transition to MD1 and S1 arrival at F1.
scenario_results.name: f3_ps1_md1_arrive_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies reset from an upward motion state forces floor 1 stop regardless of current travel context.
scenario_results.name: reset_from_up_motion_forces_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies reset from a downward motion state forces floor 1 stop regardless of current travel context.
scenario_results.name: reset_from_down_motion_forces_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies reset from a non-F1 floor context also forces floor 1 stop.
scenario_results.name: reset_from_floor_context_forces_f1

evidence: DSL defines F1, F2, F3, MU2, MU3, MD1, MD2.
DSL includes F1->MU2:PS2, F1->MU3:PS3, F2->MU3:PS3, F2->MD1:PS1, F3->MD1:PS1, F3->MD2:PS2.
DSL includes MU2->F2:S2, MU3->F3:S3, MD1->F1:S1, MD2->F2:S2.
DSL sets hbrg=1 in MU2/MU3, hbrg=-1 in MD1/MD2, and hbrg=0 in F1/F2/F3.
DSL includes [*] -> F1 and ! * -> F1 : reset.
findings.summary: The DSL closely matches the NL-described elevator FSM: required floor states, motion states, request-triggered departures, sensor-triggered arrivals, hbrg drive/stop outputs, initial F1 dispatch, and reset-to-F1 behavior are represented.

Simulation summary reports 8/8 scenarios passed.
findings.summary: Core components are covered: states, transitions, trigger events, output variable, entry actions, initial transition, and reset transition are all present and grounded.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary advisory_items_sample contains W_UNREFERENCED_VAR: Variable 'hbrg' does not affect any transition guard.
NL describes hbrg as an output that distinguishes upward drive, downward drive, and stop conditions.
No transition logic in the NL requires hbrg to guard transitions.
findings.summary: The only design diagnostic is W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for hbrg, but this appears to be an output-only variable rather than a missing guard dependency.

evidence: NL: 'A reset signal forces the controller back to floor 1 regardless of the outstanding request context.'
DSL: ! * -> F1 : reset.
sim_summary includes reset_from_up_motion_forces_f1 and reset_from_down_motion_forces_f1 scenarios passing.
findings.summary: Reset directly forces F1 from any state, including motion states. This is faithful to the NL wording but remains a physical-abstraction risk if interpreted as real elevator car position rather than controller state.

evidence: GroundingMap source_summary assumption: 'immediately checks the next destination' is represented by entering floor states with outgoing request-triggered transitions.
DSL has floor states with outgoing PS-triggered transitions and no persistent request variables.
findings.summary: The model uses event-triggered floor-state outgoing transitions to represent 'immediately checks the next destination' rather than adding explicit decision pseudostates or stored request context. This is reasonable because the NL lists trigger-based transitions and does not require request memory.

evidence: GroundingMap covers all required states, events, transitions, reset, and hbrg actions.
